liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (5 reviews): The Dark Star runs a healthy 19 minutes or so, on its own track after a short fragment; This Dark Star had not circulated before, and the band plays with vigor [2][3][6][8][12]
- **That's It For The Other One** (1 review): A fiery Other One that points toward the greater versions to come, such as 4/28/71 [4]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Good Lovin' is judged among the best the reviewer has heard [4]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-10-17.aud.linton.miller.119329.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 154 min; rated 4/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Cuts remain in Truckin' and at the starts of That's It For The Other One and Hard To Handle; other dropouts were repaired; The audience recording is quite decent for 1970; Typical of 1970 audience tapes in quality, and cleaned up from earlier circulating versions [1][2][3][4][8]

## Around the show

- An attendee found the show magical in person and drove over from Meadville, PA with friends [7]
- The show carried on into the early morning hours [7]
- First of four Cleveland Music Hall shows; it is the smaller room of the Public Auditorium [11]
- The next night's Guthrie Theater show is the only Minnesota Dead show with no recording, so this tape shows where they stood [10]
- Unlike other 1970 Dark Stars, this one has no Feelin' Groovy or Tighten Up jam [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-10-17.aud.linton.miller.119329.flac16**: taped by Jeff Linton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Unknown Mic -> Cassette Master (Mono) [1]. Also: Taped by Jeff Linton from the front row of the balcony; The encore was moved to the end of set one so the show fit on two discs [1]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Raw Sugar Art Studio: [45 Years Ago Today – Grateful Dead At Music Hall](https://clevelandrockandroll.com/45-years-ago-today-grateful-dead-at-music-hall/) [15]
